title: capacity-cost-hedge-and-deferred-hire-scenario
body:
Executive summary:
This is a working playbook that models a small set of alternative capacity/headcount phasing decisions tied to short-term price movements in cloud GPU market and projected token-price compression. Purpose is to give CFO/Product leadership a quick run-of-the-mill hedge that preserves runway while keeping critical infra hires on path.

Key objectives:
- Quantify P&L and runway impact of a 3-month hiring pause with a targeted reserve for burst GPU capacity.
- Show tradeoffs vs a mild price increase (per-token) and vs aggressive price compression.
- Output one recommended contingency plan with triggers and ownerable next steps.

Assumptions (working):
- Baseline monthly spend (Mar 2026): fixed infra + sustained GPU ops = $1.8M (incl. committed Dedicated pool and hosted API footprint).
- Average fully-loaded new-engineer cost (first-year) = $280k (salary + benefits + ramp overhead across 12 months) => monthly run-rate per hire ~ $23.3k in year1.
- Burst GPU reserve (spot-style or short-term committed) incremental cost = $150k/month when active.
- Token price scenarios considered relative to baseline per-token yield: Flat (0%), -18% (price compression), +10% (price increase passed to customers).
- Hiring plan baseline (Q2–Q4 2026): 24 hires (mix of infra, SRE, serving runtime), ramp equally over 3 quarters = 8 hires/quarter.

Scenarios modeled (high level):
1) Baseline (no action): continue hires + maintain reserve at current level.
   - Hires: +8/qtr Q2,Q3,Q4
   - Runway delta: 0
   - Notes: highest product velocity, highest burn.

2) Deferred-hire + reserve hedge (recommended staging): 3-month hiring pause on non-critical roles; reallocate $700k of monthly hiring budget to a burst reserve and contingency fund.
   - Hires paused: 6 deferred hires in Q2 (non-urgent infra/tooling), remaining 18 hires spread Q3–Q4 (+9/qtr).
   - Reserve: activate additional burst reserve for 3 months (cost ~$150k/mo).
   - Estimated short-term runway extension: ~2.8 months (conservative)
   - Product impact: moderate delay on low-priority infra initiatives; critical SLO hires still hired.

3) Price-compression shock (-18% revenue per token): combine hiring pause with targeted cost cuts in non-personnel OpEx (absorb $200k/mo) + modest slowdown in our marketing spend.
   - Hires paused: same 6 as scenario 2 plus 2 sales hires; total deferred hires = 8 in Q2.
   - Runway extension: ~4.1 months (estimated)
   - Risk: customer churn if we cannot maintain service improvements; requires mitigation.

Quick sensitivity table (rounded):
Scenario | Monthly burn delta | Net runway change (months) | Notes
Baseline | +$0 | 0
Deferred-hire | -$720k/month (net after reserve activation) | +2.8
Compression + cuts | -$1.05M/month | +4.1

Headcount phasing (table-style lines):
Role | Baseline hires Q2/Q3/Q4 | Deferred plan Q2/Q3/Q4
SRE/Oncall | 2/2/2 | 2/1/1
Serving-runtime Eng | 3/3/3 | 2/3/3
Infra Eng (non-critical) | 2/2/2 | 0/3/3
Data/Applied ML | 1/1/1 | 0/1/2
Sales/CS | 0/1/1 | 0/1/1
Total | 8/9/9 | 4/9/10

Cost math notes (quick):
- Deferred 6 hires in Q2 => immediate cashflow savings roughly: 6 * $23.3k = ~$139.8k/month in Q2. But realistic vacancy/offer leakage and ramp pushes that to ~ $110k/month.
- Re-allocating budget to burst reserve: assume we convert part of hiring pipeline budget (one-time hiring costs, recruiter fees) to build a $700k contingency pool across three months.
- If token price compresses 18%, hosted revenue pressure will likely manifest with ~1.2x amplification on our burn over 4–6 months unless we take product-level price or feature gating.

Operational tradeoffs and mitigations:
- Keep 40% of paused roles as interview pipelines (soft-offers) so we can resume quickly within 6–8 weeks if demand rebounds.
- Use targeted internal re-prioritization: shift 2 infra FTEs temporarily to critical SLO work to avoid outages.
- Negotiate short-term supplier credits for cloud commit schedule to smooth spike risk.

Trigger matrix (ownerable):
- If billed token price realization drops >= 12% vs baseline for two consecutive weeks => finance-led cadence (Marisol) runs compression playbook; pause non-critical offers within 3 business days.
- If gross margin erosion > 6% in trailing 30-day window => escalate to CFO + Product for price/feature gating decisions.
- If customer latency SLOs degrade (>2% error budget over 2 weeks) => cancel any further deferrals for SRE hires and reallocate contingency.

Open questions / To do:
- Confirm revised average hire cost with People Ops (ask Priya for regional comp adjustments).
- Validate burst GPU pricing with Ops team (Daniel to confirm spot vs short commitments pricing ladder).
- Build a one-page playbook for sales-led accounts that may need temporary credits (owner: Liam).

Notes to self / meeting prep bits:
- This doc is intentionally terse — need a single-slide summary (one metric: runway months saved) for Monday exec sync.
- Flag dependency FIN-3421 (linked) for legal review if we make one-off customer credits.

Next steps (owners + timing):
- People Ops comp check (Priya) by 2026-03-15.
- Ops GPU rate validation (Daniel) by 2026-03-17.
- Draft slide and exec one-pager (Marisol + Liam) by 2026-03-18.

References and links:
- Linked Confluence hedge note (see linked_artifacts)
- Jira piece FIN-3421 contains the committed GPU schedule and vendor contract summary
- PR in ops repo with short-term capacity scripts (linked above)

If we need to make this more formal for Q2 board review, convert to a spreadsheet with the per-hire P&L by month and a waterfall chart for runway. For now — this is a working financial playbook to present to Product and CFO.

-- Marisol
